title: Reproducible research
deck: A paper monorepo where every figure comes from a versioned pipeline. If a result does not reproduce, it does not go into the manuscript.

links.label: Paper: potato prices (Frontiers in Sust. Food Syst.)

blocks.text: In applied research, paper tables are often copied by hand from notebooks nobody can run again. When a reviewer asks for a change, redoing the numbers takes weeks and opens the door to errors.

Each paper lives in its own folder with a `manifest.yaml` (title, target journal, authors and the status of every figure), its data, notebooks, experiments and manuscript. Shared scripts build the PDF, validate DOIs and bibliography, check layout against the journal guide and sync deliverables.

blocks.source:
flowchart LR
  D[(Peruvian public data)] --> N[Executable notebooks]
  N --> X[Versioned experiments]
  X --> O[Outputs: tables and figures]
  O --> M[Manuscript]
  MF[manifest.yaml] --> M
  M --> CI{CI}
  CI --> V1[Validate DOIs and bibliography]
  CI --> V2[Check journal layout]
  CI --> V3[Tests and PDF build]

└── journal_guide.py        # reglas de cada revista destino

items: **Temporal, not random, validation.** Series are split by time to measure real generalisation, not model memory.
**Stability over minimum error.** For Canchán potatoes we chose LSTM-XGBoost for robustness, even when another model had a lower point error.
**Mixed data with FAMD.** For clinical records with numeric and categorical variables, FAMD before K-Means gave the best clustering quality.
